subject: Default capture horizon & erasure steps (requests vs outputs) — Northbridge.ai
messages:
From: Jane Smith <jane.smith@northbridge.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on what you keep by default — requests vs outputs

Hi Diego,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Northbridge is evaluating Redwood for clinical triage workflows. A couple of follow-ups from our security and procurement teams:

1) For hosted API customers in the EU region, what is the default retention horizon for: (a) raw requests (customer prompts / user input), (b) model outputs (generated answers), and (c) streaming fragments/KV-cache artifacts?
2) If we request erasure for a user or submission, what is the expected SLA and what evidence do you provide back to the customer (proof of deletion, logs, timestamps)?
3) Can we opt-out of any capture by default for certain routes during evaluation?

Can you send a short matrix we can pass to procurement/security?

Thanks,
Jane
Jane Smith
Head of Security & Partnerships, Northbridge.ai

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on what you keep by default — requests vs outputs

Hi Jane — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below and I attached a short retention matrix PDF.

Summary (hosted, EU region, default behavior):
- Raw requests (user prompts / inputs): retained by default for 30 days. This covers full request text + request metadata for debugging and quality metrics.
- Model outputs (final generated answers): retained by default for 60 days. We retain outputs slightly longer to support customer QA and regression detection.
- Streaming fragments & KV-cache artifacts: transient by default — in-host memory for up to 2 hours and persisted checkpoints (for session reconnection) are purged after 7 days unless the customer opts into longer retention.

Erasure SLA and evidence:
- For hosted customers we start a deletion job within 48 hours of an authenticated erasure request (support ticket or API call from an admin).
- Live records are removed from the primary serving/telemetry stores; tombstone markers propagate to archival backends. Final physical removal from backups and tombstones completes within 30 days; customers receive an erasure report with timestamps when the deletion job completes.

Opt-out/configuration:
- You can disable request/response capture at the route level for evaluation ("no-capture" flag) — we can set this per-route or per-API key. Dedicated/Private deployments can be configured with capture disabled by default.

Attached: redwood-retention-matrix-2027-03.pdf (breaks down regions and durations). Looping in Laura for any operational runbook details and for the erasure evidence template.

Best,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-retention-matrix-2027-03.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 12:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on what you keep by default — requests vs outputs

Hi Jane,

Quick ops clarification and the practical steps we run when a deletion is requested:

1) Verification: we verify the requestor is an authorized admin for the account (HubSpot record + account API key) — this is normally done via a short form submitted to support (link below).
2) Execution: once verified, an automated workflow kicks off that:
   - removes the records from the live index/serving cache,
   - marks the items as deleted in the retention index, and
   - issues async jobs to scrub derived artifacts (search indexes, analytics snapshots).
3) Evidence: we attach a timestamped CSV (erasure-report-<account>-<date>.csv) with object IDs and a deletion status; a second job produces a signed PDF proof-of-deletion once the archival purge completes.

Notes on streaming tokens vs final output: streaming intermediate tokens are treated as ephemeral. Only if streaming is configured to persist (customer opt-in for session replay) will those fragments be stored beyond the 2-hour in-memory window.

If you want, we can run through a mock erasure during the pilot and provide the signed proof to validate the flow.

Laura Bennett
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Related link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cRetentionMatrix

1) Retention customization: yes — for evaluation we can set request retention to 7 days and keep outputs at 60 days. We document the per-route retention in the SOW.
2) Erasure evidence: attached a template (northbridge-erasure-evidence-template.xlsx) with the columns we provide (object_id, capture_type, original_timestamp, deletion_job_id, deletion_started_at, deletion_completed_at, backend_status).
